newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, market seen bottoming out.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, market seen bottoming out.

text.p: Slovenian shares tumbled 1.03 percent on Wednesday, in decline for the third session in a row, but traders predicted the market should bottom out soon.
The SBI index fell 13.75 points to 1,321.19. The index has fallen 2.2 percent so far this week.

"Prices are already so low that they are not likely to fall much further. It is not impossible that even domestic investors could start buying now on such prices," Jasna Zontar, a trader at brokerage Modra said.
"The first thing that could bring optimism to our market is some clarification of the mystery surrounding foreign investment, but I do not expect that to happen before mid-May," Zontar added.

In February the central bank blocked foreign portfolio investment by saying that international investors would have to open special custody accounts at Slovenian banks in order to trade in Slovenian shares.
Banks said first custodian accounts could be opened by the end of April or the beginning of May.
Turnover fell to 45.6 million tolars from 82.9 million. Overall six shares fell, six rose and three were flat, while 12 were untraded.
Warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC had the biggest turnover, falling 3.65 percent to 13,180 tolars on volume of 890 shares for total turnover of 11.7 million tolars.
Brokerage Dadas led the day's decliners, tumbling 7.3 percent to 7,500 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
Preferred shares of Kovinotehna were the top gainers, firming 7.53 percent to 500 tolars on volume of 10 shares.
Mercator was the most actively traded share on the over-the-counter (OTC) section of the Ljubljana bourse, easing 0.16 percent to 4,429 tolars on volume of 4,211 shares.
"Today's volume in Mercator was too low to show where its share price will move in the short term," one broker said.
